items.title: Índio da Cuíca :: Zing Zing
items.summary: At 70, Brazilian percussionist Índio da Cuíca reinvented himself as one of the country’s strangest musical voices. His cuíca—usually a squeaky rhythmic accent—is transformed into a melodic instrument of uncanny virtuosity, set against samba, capoeira, Afro-Brazilian spirituals and warped pop forms. On Zing Zing , that “avant-traditional” vision expands further, as cavaquinho, pandeiro, berimbau and bandolim collide with guitars, synths and samples. Samba music from some parallel universe. The post Índio da Cuíca :: Zing Zing first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .

items.title: Maddy Prior & June Tabor’s Silly Sisters at 50
items.summary: Maddy Prior and June Tabor’s Silly Sisters is a magical hinge album, a meeting of two transcendent voices and a jolly band of British folk masters. Recorded in 1976 but somehow outside of time, its ancient songs, close harmonies, and loose, luminous performances summon something older than the British folk revival itself. Fifty years on, it remains a timeless gem hiding in plain sight: raw, sophisticated, mysterious, and still not quite given its due. The post Maddy Prior & June Tabor’s Silly Sisters at 50 first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .

items.title: Duncan Sheik Dead At 56
items.summary: Duncan Sheik has died. The New Jersey-born singer-songwriter, best known for the pop-rock hit “Barely Breathing” and the musical Spring Awakening , passed away last night in a hospital in Manhattan. His mother, Suzanne Sheik, told the New York Times the cause of death was cardiac arrest. "Duncan was a father, husband, son, brother, and friend," reads a statement shared on his social media. "He will be remembered for his sensitivity, wit, inteligence, and depth of spirit he brought to those who knew and loved him." Sheik was 56.
